checklist.evidence: Use a CRDT library such as Yjs (most mature) or Automerge. The main alternative is OT... Pick a CRDT unless you have a specific reason not to.
Decide which blocks and formatting you support (paragraphs, headings, lists, links and so on).
generate random edits on several copies, apply them in random orders, and confirm every copy matches.
store each edit as it arrives, periodically combine them into a full snapshot, and load "snapshot + recent edits" when a document opens.
reconnect automatically with increasing delays... pass updates between servers through a pub/sub system (such as Redis), or route each document's users to the same server.
save a local copy in the browser (IndexedDB), allow editing while offline, and merge automatically on reconnect.
A viewer's edits must be rejected by the server, not just hidden in the interface.
Undo should reverse only your own changes... restoring an old one (by applying it as a new change, not by rewriting history).
Presence: other users' cursors and selections... Yjs's awareness feature makes this fairly cheap.
Merging comes first because a mistake there means lost or corrupted documents.
Backups, document size limits and cleanup (trimming old history from very large documents).
Changing this later means migrating every stored document.
